records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the year the sixth, in the sixth [month], on the fifth of the month, I [was] sitting in my house, and [the] elders of Judah sitting before me, and fell upon me there [the] hand of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: On the fifth day of the sixth month, in the sixth year, as I sat in my house with the elders of Judah seated before me, the hand of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} fell on me there.

L.1: And it came about in the sixth year, in the sixth [month], on the fifth [day] of the month, as I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting before me, that the hand of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} fell upon me there.

R.1: It was the sixth year of our exile, the fifth day of the sixth month. I was at home, and the elders of Judah were sitting with me. Then the power of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} came on me.

decisions.choice: the sixth year, the sixth month, the fifth day: about September 592 BC
decisions.reason: Ezekiel counts the years from the exile of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (1:2), and the months from the spring. This vision comes about fourteen months after the first one (1:1-2). On the usual reckoning the date falls in September 592 BC, some six years before Jerusalem fell. Chapters 8-11 are one vision, and 11:24-25 closes it.

decisions.choice: the elders of Judah: leaders of the exiles in Babylon
decisions.reason: The exiles kept their own elders in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:1). They come to sit before the prophet again in 14:1 and 20:1, to hear a word from the LORD. What follows is a vision of what their fellow leaders in Jerusalem are doing (8:11-12).

decisions.choice: the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me: God's power took hold of the prophet and the vision began
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses this expression when a vision or a word comes on him with force (1:3; 3:14, 22; 37:1; 40:1). Here the verb is "fell", a stronger word than the usual "was upon me", and only 11:5 uses it again.

decisions.choice: the power of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} came on me
alternatives: the hand of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} fell on me
decisions.reason: Readable says "the power of the LORD came on me", the settled wording for this expression in Ezekiel (as 2 Kings 3:15). Literal and Balanced keep "the hand" and the verb "fell" (m3).

decisions.choice: the sixth year of our exile
alternatives: the sixth year
decisions.reason: Readable says from what point the years are counted, as 1:2 does, so that the date is not taken as the sixth year of a king's reign (m1).

records.heading: The image of jealousy

records.source: וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה דְמוּת֙ כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֔שׁ מִמַּרְאֵ֥ה מָתְנָ֛יו וּלְמַ֖טָּה אֵ֑שׁ וּמִמָּתְנָ֣יו וּלְמַ֔עְלָה כְּמַרְאֵה־זֹ֖הַר כְּעֵ֥ין הַחַשְׁמַֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and behold, a likeness like [the] appearance of fire; from [the] appearance of his waist and downward, fire, and from his waist and upward, like [the] appearance of brightness, like [the] gleam of the amber.
pieces: I looked, and I saw something that looked like fire. From what appeared to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist down there was fire, and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist up there was something like a radiance, shining like gleaming metal.

L.2: And I looked, and look, a likeness like the appearance of fire! From the appearance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist and down [was] fire, and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist and up [was something] like the appearance of brightness, like the gleam of amber.

R.2: I looked and saw something that looked like fire. From what seemed to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist down, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was fire. From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} seemed to glow brightly, like shining metal.

decisions.choice: the figure of fire is the one Ezekiel saw on the throne in 1:26-27, and he speaks as God
alternatives: an angel who guides the prophet, as the man of bronze in 40:3
decisions.reason: The description repeats 1:27 almost word for word: fire from the waist down, brightness and the gleam of amber from the waist up. That figure was "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD" (1:28). In 8:6 the one who speaks to Ezekiel calls the temple "my sanctuary", so the voice in this vision is God's own. Ezekiel still describes him only by likenesses (see 1:28).

decisions.choice: fire: the Hebrew text
alternatives: a man: the Greek (Septuagint) reading, which needs a change of one vowel letter in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "a likeness like the appearance of fire". The Septuagint has "the likeness of a man", which matches the human form on the throne in 1:26-27, and the words for "fire" and "man" differ by a single letter in Hebrew. The Hebrew text is kept, since a figure of fire also fits 1:27; the sense is the same either way, because the fire is in the shape of a body with a waist.

decisions.choice: amber: the gleaming substance of 1:4 and 1:27
decisions.reason: The word is used only in 1:4, 1:27 and here, and its exact sense is uncertain; see 1:4. Here, as there, it describes a bright, glowing color, not the figure's material.

decisions.choice: something that looked like fire; what appeared to be (B); something that looked like fire; what seemed to be (R)
alternatives: a likeness like the appearance of fire; the appearance of his waist
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Ezekiel's doubled hedge word for word. Balanced and Readable shorten it but keep a hedge ("looked like", "seemed"), as the settled wording requires (see 1:28). Balanced says "gleaming metal" and Readable "shining metal" for amber, as in 1:4.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ׀בֵּֽין־הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל־פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And he stretched out [the] form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head, and lifted me [the] Spirit between the earth and between the heavens and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of God, to [the] entrance of [the] gate of the inner [court] that faces north, where there [was the] seat of the image of the jealousy that provokes to jealousy.
pieces: He reached out something that looked like a hand and took hold of me by a lock of my hair. The Spirit lifted me up between earth and sky and, in visions from God, brought me to Jerusalem, to the doorway of the inner court's north gate, where the image of jealousy stood, the image that provokes jealousy.

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put out the form of a hand and seized me by a lock of my head; and the Spirit raised me up between the earth and the heavens and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of God, to the entrance of the gate of the inner [court] that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy, [was].

R.3: Something that looked like a hand reached out and took me by the hair. Then the Spirit lifted me up between the earth and the sky. In these visions from God, the Spirit took me to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard. That was where the image of jealousy stood, the idol that made God jealous.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: God's Spirit, who carries the prophet
alternatives: a wind that lifts the prophet
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can mean wind, breath or spirit; see 2:2. The same thing happens in 3:12, 14 and 11:1, 24, where the spirit lifts Ezekiel and carries him. Since the journey takes place "in visions of God" and 11:24 calls it "the Spirit of God", the Spirit of God is meant, though "wind" is possible.

decisions.choice: in visions of God: visions that God gave, as in 1:1 and 40:2
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is taken to Jerusalem in a vision, not in body: at the end he is back among the exiles and tells them what he saw (11:24-25), and the elders are still sitting before him. The form of the hand and the lock of hair belong to the vision too.

decisions.choice: the image of jealousy: an idol set up at the temple gate, which roused the LORD's jealousy
alternatives: an image of the goddess Asherah, like the one King Manasseh set in the temple (2 Kings 21:7)
decisions.reason: The LORD is "a jealous God" who will not share his people's worship with other gods (Exodus 20:4-5; Deuteronomy 32:16, 21). The word for the image is rare; it is used for an idol in Deuteronomy 4:16 and for the idol Manasseh put in the house of God (2 Chronicles 33:7, 15). That idol was an image of Asherah (2 Kings 21:7), and Ezekiel may mean that one or another like it. The text names no god, so neither does the translation.

decisions.choice: the gate of the inner court that faces north
alternatives: the inner gate that faces north
decisions.reason: The word "inner" is feminine and probably refers to the court (as in 8:16), not to the gate. The north gate led from the outer court into the inner court where the altar stood; 8:5 calls it "the altar gate".

decisions.choice: the idol that made God jealous
alternatives: the image of the jealousy that provokes to jealousy
decisions.reason: Readable says whose jealousy is meant and that the image is an idol, so the reader is not left with a riddle (m3). It keeps the name "the image of jealousy", which returns in 8:5.

records.source: וְהִ֨נֵּה־שָׁ֔ם כְּב֖וֹד אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּמַּרְאֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי בַּבִּקְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And behold, there [was the] glory of [the] God of Israel, like the vision that I had seen in the plain.
pieces: And there was the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it in the vision in the plain.

L.4: And look, the glory of the God of Israel [was] there, like the vision that I had seen in the plain.

R.4: And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel. It looked just as it had in the vision I saw in the open plain.

decisions.choice: the glory of the God of Israel: the glory Ezekiel saw by the Kebar and again in the plain (1:28; 3:22-23)
decisions.reason: The same glory that appeared to Ezekiel in Babylon is still present in the temple, a few steps from the idol at the gate. In chapters 10-11 it will leave the temple and the city (10:18-19; 11:22-23).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שָׂא־נָ֥א עֵינֶ֖יךָ דֶּ֣רֶךְ צָפ֑וֹנָה וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ צָפ֔וֹנָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה מִצָּפוֹן֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ סֵ֛מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה בַּבִּאָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, lift up now your eyes [the] way of [the] north. And I lifted up my eyes [the] way of [the] north, and behold, north of [the] gate of the altar, this image of the jealousy, in the entrance.
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, look toward the north." So I looked toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, in the entrance itself, was this image of jealousy.

L.5: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, lift up now your eyes toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and look, north of the gate of the altar [was] this image of jealousy, in the entrance.

R.5: He said to me, "Son of man, look toward the north." So I looked north. There in the entrance, north of the gate by the altar, I saw the idol, the image of jealousy.

decisions.choice: son of man: a human being, God's address to Ezekiel (see 2:1)
decisions.reason: God addresses Ezekiel this way throughout the book; the note at 2:1 explains it.

decisions.choice: the altar gate: the north gate into the inner court, where the altar stood
decisions.reason: The idol of 8:3 stood in the gateway itself, so that everyone who went in to the altar passed it. The word for "entrance" is found only here.

decisions.choice: look; I looked
alternatives: lift up your eyes; I lifted up my eyes
decisions.reason: "Lift up your eyes" is a common Hebrew way of saying "look". Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable say "look".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲרֹאֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה מָ֣ה הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֑ים תּוֹעֵב֨וֹת גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀עֹשִׂ֣ים פֹּ֗ה לְרָֽחֳקָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, [are] seeing you what they [are] doing, abominations great that [the] house of Israel [is] doing here, to be far from upon my sanctuary? And yet you will again see abominations greater.
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see the things they are doing, the terrible detestable practices that the house of Israel is committing here, which will drive {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} far from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary? But you will see even greater detestable practices."

L.6: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, are you seeing what they are doing, great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, so that [I] go far from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary? Yet you will see greater abominations still."

R.6: He said to me, "Son of man, can you see what they are doing? The people of Israel are doing terrible, disgusting things here. They will drive {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} far away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own temple. But you will see things even more disgusting than these."

decisions.choice: abominations: practices the LORD finds detestable, above all the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: See 5:9. The word is used of the idol worship and other practices that the LORD hates (Deuteronomy 18:12). It runs through this vision like a refrain (8:6, 9, 13, 15, 17), and each scene is worse than the one before.

decisions.choice: so that the LORD goes far from his sanctuary
alternatives: so that they themselves are far from the sanctuary
to keep far from the sanctuary, that is, in rebellion against it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "to be far from my sanctuary" and does not say who will be far. Read with what follows, it points to God: the glory leaves the temple in 10:18-19 and 11:22-23. It can also mean that the people, by these practices, are putting themselves far from the sanctuary (as 11:15 uses the same verb of the people).

decisions.choice: detestable practices (B); disgusting things (R)
alternatives: abominations
decisions.reason: This is the settled wording for this word in Ezekiel: "abomination" at Literal, "detestable practice" at Balanced, "disgusting thing" at Readable (as Deuteronomy 18:12). "Great" is "terrible" at Balanced and Readable, since it describes how serious they are.

decisions.choice: The people of Israel; than these
alternatives: the house of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Israel" for "the house of Israel" and splits the question into short sentences. It adds "than these", which 8:15 says outright.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח הֶֽחָצֵ֑ר וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֹר־אֶחָ֖ד בַּקִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: And he brought me to [the] entrance of the court, and I looked, and behold, a hole, one, in the wall.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the entrance of the court, and when I looked, I saw a hole in the wall.

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the entrance of the court; and I looked, and look, a hole in the wall.

R.7: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me to the entrance of the courtyard. I looked and saw a hole in the wall.

decisions.choice: a hole in the wall: the way into a hidden room
decisions.reason: The next scene is done out of sight, "in the dark" (8:12). Ezekiel has to make the hole larger to get in (8:8).

records.heading: The elders in the dark

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֖ם חֲתָר־נָ֣א בַקִּ֑יר וָאֶחְתֹּ֣ר בַּקִּ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֖ה פֶּ֥תַח אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, dig now in the wall. And I dug in the wall, and behold, an entrance, one.
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was a doorway.

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, dig now through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and look, a doorway.

R.8: He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall and found a doorway.

decisions.choice: dig through the wall: the same verb as in the sign of 12:5, 7, 12
decisions.reason: Here Ezekiel digs into a hidden shrine in the vision. In chapter 12 he digs through a wall to act out the exile that will follow, and the king digs his way out of the city.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֹּ֤א וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־הַתּוֹעֵב֣וֹת הָרָע֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם עֹשִׂ֖ים פֹּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Go in and see the abominations, the evil, that they [are] doing here.
pieces: He said to me, "Go in and see the wicked detestable practices they are committing here."

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Go in and see the evil abominations that they are committing here."

R.9: He said to me, "Go in and see the evil, disgusting things they are doing here."

records.source: וָאָבוֹא֮ וָֽאֶרְאֶה֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה כָל־תַּבְנִ֜ית רֶ֤מֶשׂ וּבְהֵמָה֙ שֶׁ֔קֶץ וְכָל־גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מְחֻקֶּ֥ה עַל־הַקִּ֖יר סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And I went in and looked, and behold, every form of creeping thing and beast, detestable thing, and all [the] idols of [the] house of Israel, carved on the wall all around, all around.
pieces: So I went in and looked, and there, carved all around on the wall, were all kinds of creeping things and beasts, detestable things, and all the idols of the house of Israel.

L.10: So I went in and looked, and look, every form of creeping thing and beast, a detestable thing, and all the filthy idols of the house of Israel, carved on the wall all around.

R.10: So I went in and looked. All around the walls were carvings of every kind of crawling creature and of unclean, disgusting animals. All the idols of the people of Israel were carved there too.

decisions.choice: every form of creeping thing and beast, a detestable thing: the images the law forbids
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 4:16-18 forbids making the form of any beast or any creeping thing for worship. The word "detestable thing" is the word for unclean creatures in Leviticus 11:10-42. Worship of animal figures was known in Egypt, and Judah's kings at this time looked to Egypt for help, but the text does not say where these images came from.

decisions.choice: idols: the word Ezekiel uses with contempt for idols (see 6:4)
decisions.reason: See 6:4.

decisions.choice: carved: cut or drawn into the wall
alternatives: painted
decisions.reason: The word means something engraved or drawn. In 23:14 the same word is used of figures on a wall painted in red.

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word in Ezekiel (see 6:4).

decisions.choice: unclean, disgusting animals
alternatives: beasts, a detestable thing
decisions.reason: Readable says that "detestable" here is the word for unclean animals (m1).

records.source: וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י בֵֽית־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל וְיַאֲזַנְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־שָׁפָ֜ן עֹמֵ֤ד בְּתוֹכָם֙ עֹמְדִ֣ים לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִ֥ישׁ מִקְטַרְתּ֖וֹ בְּיָד֑וֹ וַעֲתַ֥ר עֲנַֽן־הַקְּטֹ֖רֶת עֹלֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And seventy men from [the] elders of [the] house of Israel, and Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing in their midst, standing before them, and each his censer in his hand, and [the] fragrance of [the] cloud of the incense going up.
pieces: In front of them stood seventy of the elders of the house of Israel, and Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stood in the middle of them. Every man held his censer, and a fragrant cloud of incense rose up.

L.11: And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing in their midst, and each man [had] his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was going up.

R.11: Seventy of the elders of Israel were standing in front of these carvings. Jaazaniah son of Shaphan was standing among them. Each of them held a pan for burning incense, and sweet-smelling smoke was rising from the incense.

decisions.choice: seventy elders: the number of the elders who once saw the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Seventy elders went up the mountain with Moses and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:1, 9-11), and seventy elders received a share of the spirit that was on Moses (Numbers 11:16, 24-25). Now seventy elders stand before images of animals.

decisions.choice: Jaazaniah son of Shaphan: probably from the family of Shaphan, King Josiah's secretary
alternatives: an otherwise unknown Shaphan
decisions.reason: Shaphan was the royal secretary under Josiah (2 Kings 22:3), and his sons Ahikam and Gemariah and his grandson Gedaliah supported Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:24; 36:10-12; 39:14). If this Jaazaniah is another son of that Shaphan, even a family known for loyalty to the LORD has a man among the worshipers. The name was common, and the link is not certain. He is a different man from Jaazaniah son of Azzur in 11:1.

decisions.choice: censers and incense: burning incense was the priests' task
decisions.reason: A censer was a pan for carrying burning coals, on which incense was placed. Offering incense belonged to the priests (Numbers 16:1-40; 2 Chronicles 26:16-20), but here the elders do it, and to images.

decisions.choice: in front of these carvings; a pan for burning incense
alternatives: before them; his censer
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are (the carvings of 8:10) and what a censer is.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר זִקְנֵ֤י בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ אִ֖ישׁ בְּחַדְרֵ֣י מַשְׂכִּית֑וֹ כִּ֣י אֹמְרִ֗ים אֵ֤ין יְהוָה֙ רֹאֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔נוּ עָזַ֥ב יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Have you seen, son of man, what [the] elders of [the] house of Israel [are] doing in the dark, each in [the] rooms of his image? For [they are] saying, Yahweh [is] not seeing us; has forsaken Yahweh the land.
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel practice in darkness, each in the room of his own carved image? They say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not see us; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has abandoned the land.'"

L.12: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Have you seen, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in darkness, each man in the rooms of his carved image? For they say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is not seeing us; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has forsaken the land.'"

R.12: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what the elders of Israel are doing in the dark? Each of them is in a room with his own idol. They say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not see us. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has left the land.'"

decisions.choice: the rooms of his carved image: private shrines, each with its own figure
alternatives: the carved figures on the walls of the one room, which each man treated as his own
decisions.reason: The word for "image" is used of a figured stone set up for worship (Leviticus 26:1; Numbers 33:52). "In the dark" means in secret, away from the public. Whether there were many rooms or one room with many figures is not clear.

decisions.choice: "The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land": the excuse for turning to other gods
decisions.reason: After King Jehoiachin and the leading citizens were taken to Babylon in 597 BC, these leaders conclude that the LORD has abandoned the land and pays no attention to it, so they look to other powers. In 9:9 the LORD quotes these words back as the reason for the judgment.

decisions.choice: a room with his own idol
alternatives: the rooms of his carved image
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the image is an idol (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִֽׂים׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Again you will see abominations greater that they [are] doing.
pieces: He said to me, "You will see them committing even greater detestable practices."

L.13: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "You will see still greater abominations that they are committing."

R.13: He said to me, "You will see them doing things that are even more disgusting."

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל־פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל־הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־הַתַּמּֽוּז׃ס
records.gloss: And he brought me to [the] entrance of [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh which [is] toward the north, and behold, there the women sitting, weeping for the Tammuz.
pieces: Next {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the doorway of the north gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Women were sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that [is] toward the north; and look, there the women were sitting, weeping for Tammuz.

R.14: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me to the entrance of the north gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Women were sitting there, weeping for the god Tammuz.

decisions.choice: Tammuz: a Mesopotamian god whose death was mourned each year
decisions.reason: Tammuz (Dumuzi in Sumerian) was a god of shepherds and of growing things in Mesopotamia. Stories told that he died and went down to the world of the dead, and every year women mourned for him with laments. A month of the later Jewish calendar, in early summer, still bears his name. Here the mourning has come to the gate of the LORD's own house. The Hebrew has "the Tammuz", with the article, as some names of gods have it.

decisions.choice: the god Tammuz
alternatives: Tammuz
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tammuz is a god, which most readers would not know (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלַ֖י הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָ֑ם ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Have you seen, son of man? Again you will see abominations greater than these.
pieces: He said to me, "Do you see this, son of man? You will see even greater detestable practices than these."

L.15: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? Again you will see greater abominations than these."

R.15: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this? You will see things even more disgusting than these."

records.heading: Bowing to the sun

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל־חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה־פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל־הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And he brought me into [the] court of [the] house of Yahweh, the inner, and behold, [at the] entrance of [the] temple of Yahweh, between the porch and between the altar, about twenty and five men, their backs toward [the] temple of Yahweh and their faces eastward, and they bowing down eastward to the sun.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me into the inner court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There, at the doorway of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, between the porch and the altar, stood about twenty-five men. They had turned their backs on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and were facing east, bowing down to the sun in the east.

L.16: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me into the inner court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and look, at the doorway to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, between the porch and the altar, about twenty-five men, their backs to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and their faces eastward; and they were bowing down eastward to the sun.

R.16: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me into the inner courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. At the entrance to the temple, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men. They had turned their backs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and were facing east. They were bowing down to worship the sun as it rose in the east.

decisions.choice: backs to the temple, bowing to the sun: worship of the sun, done by turning away from the LORD
decisions.reason: The temple faced east, so anyone who faced the rising sun in its court stood with his back to the LORD's house (compare 2 Chronicles 29:6). The law forbade bowing to the sun, moon and stars (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3). King Josiah had removed the horses and chariots dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance (2 Kings 23:5, 11), but the practice had returned.

decisions.choice: between the porch and the altar: the part of the court where the priests stood
alternatives: ordinary worshipers
decisions.reason: This is the place where the priests were to weep and pray (Joel 2:17). That the men stand there suggests they were priests, though the text does not say so. A different group of twenty-five men appears in 11:1.

decisions.choice: bowing down: an unusual form of the verb
decisions.reason: The form of the verb is not the usual one and may mix two spellings; the sense, "they were bowing down", is clear.

decisions.choice: the porch
alternatives: the portico
the vestibule
decisions.reason: "The porch" is the published wording for the entrance hall of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:3) and the same phrase "between the porch and the altar" (Joel 2:17).

decisions.choice: bowing down to worship the sun as it rose in the east
alternatives: bowing down eastward to the sun
decisions.reason: Readable says that the bowing is worship and that facing east means facing the rising sun (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָם֒ הֲנָקֵל֙ לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה מֵעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת־הַתּוֹעֵב֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשׂוּ־פֹ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלְא֨וּ אֶת־הָאָ֜רֶץ חָמָ֗ס וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ לְהַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי וְהִנָּ֛ם שֹׁלְחִ֥ים אֶת־הַזְּמוֹרָ֖ה אֶל־אַפָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Have you seen, son of man? Is it light for [the] house of Judah from doing the abominations that they have done here, that they have filled the land [with] violence and turned again to provoke me? And behold them, sending the branch to their nose.
pieces: He said to me, "Do you see this, son of man? Is it not enough that the house of Judah commits the detestable practices it has committed here? Must they also fill the land with violence and provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger again and again? Look, they are putting the branch to their nose!

L.17: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? Is it a light matter for the house of Judah to commit the abominations that they have committed here, that they have filled the land [with] violence and provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again and again? And look, they are putting the branch to their nose!

R.17: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this? The people of Judah are doing these disgusting things here. But that is not enough for them. They also fill the land with violence and make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry again and again. Look at them! They are holding a branch up to their noses!

decisions.choice: is it a light thing ... that they have filled the land with violence: the abominations were not enough; they added violence
alternatives: is it a light thing ...? For they have filled the land with violence
decisions.reason: The question means that the house of Judah treats these abominations as a small matter, and on top of them has filled the land with violence. The word "that" can also begin a new reason ("for"); the sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: violence: injustice and bloodshed among the people
decisions.reason: Ezekiel sets wrong done to people beside wrong done to God: the land is full of bloodshed (7:23; 9:9). The worship of other gods and the violence go together.

decisions.choice: putting the branch to their nose: a gesture whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: a rite of worship, holding a branch or twig to the face before the sun
an insulting or obscene gesture toward God
"to my nose", a stench sent up to God, a reading Jewish tradition records as the original wording
decisions.reason: The words are clear but the practice is not. It may have been part of the sun worship of 8:16, in which worshipers held up a branch, or a gesture of contempt. Jewish tradition lists this verse among places where the scribes are said to have changed "my nose" to "their nose" out of reverence; if so, the people are sending an offense up to God himself. No reading is certain, so the translation keeps the words as they stand.

decisions.choice: Is it not enough ... that they must also (B); But that is not enough for them (R)
alternatives: Is it a light thing
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a light thing". Balanced and Readable say what the question means (m1).

records.source: וְגַם־אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא־תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And also I will act in wrath; will not spare my eye, and not I will have pity; and they will call in my ears [with] a voice loud, and not I will hear them.
pieces: So I too will act in wrath. I will not look on them with pity or spare them. Though they cry out in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."

L.18: And I too will act in wrath; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye will not pity, and I will not spare; and [though] they cry in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."

R.18: So I will act in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger. I will not feel sorry for them or show them mercy. They will shout to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help, but I will not listen to them."

decisions.choice: my eye will not pity, and I will not spare: the words of 5:11 and 7:4, 9 (see 5:11)
decisions.reason: The same words close the scenes of judgment in 5:11 and 7:4, 9, and they return in 9:5 and 9:10, where the judgment begins.

decisions.choice: though they cry ... I will not listen: their cry for help will come too late
decisions.reason: The verse joins the clauses with "and"; the sense is "though they cry, I will not listen". The leaders who said "the LORD does not see us" (8:12) will find that the LORD does not hear them.

decisions.choice: I will not look on them with pity or spare them (B); I will not feel sorry for them or show them mercy (R)
alternatives: my eye will not pity, and I will not spare
decisions.reason: The settled wording of 5:11 and 7:4, 9 at each level, with "them" for "you". Literal keeps the idiom of the eye.
